notes:
Account summary: mid-market product analytics SaaS. Started with Hosted API sandbox (Q4 2025) for feature flags + search rerank. Positive perf results: p95 latency ~120ms for 128-token chat tests on hosted. Moved to Dedicated evaluation after spike concerns and compliance asks. Wants VPC Dedicated with customer-managed VPC peering.

Recent timeline (bullets / shorthand):
- 2025-12-02: first inbound trial signup (Hosted credits). AE assigned (Jordan)
- 2026-01-14: Hosted API demo + integration call; devs ran embedding recall test (Fireflies ff_2026-02-18)
- 2026-02-18: internal POC kickoff (30d). baseline throughput target: 100 concurrent live chat sessions, 25k embeddings/day.
- 2026-02-25: Dedicated architecture walkthrough w/ SE (Maya). discussed reserved GPU pool sizing and autoscale policies.
- 2026-03-02: Pricing/ops review — they requested firm commit tiers, burst rules, overage cadence (see drive doc).
- 2026-03-08: Legal/Procurement pre-RFQ questions sent; security KBA in progress (Jira INF-1129).
- 2026-03-10: Executive sponsorship call; confirmed fiscal Q2 budget window and preference for 12-month term with ramp schedule.

POC / Technical notes:
- Workload mix: 60% chat (low-latency short-turn dialog), 25% embeddings (batch jobs), 15% reranking/summarization (mid-length).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for chat (they want <200ms ideally). Throughput SLO: sustain 100 conc sessions, burst to 250 for peak hours.
- Perf from hosted: good for prototyping. Dedicated expected to reduce cost/unit and give capacity isolation. Need KV/prefix caching assurances for low tail latencies.
- Model preferences: open models first (Redwood catalog), fallback to smaller quantized variants for low-cost routes. Wants model routing policy based on latency vs cost tiers.

Commercial / Pricing negotiation notes (focus topic):
- They want a 12-month Dedicated commit. Proposed structures discussed: token-based committed units vs reserved GPU-hours.
- Galewood preference: commit measured in "monthly token-equivalent" with quarterly true-ups. Proposal A from Redwood: 3-tier commit (base, burst-pack, buffer credits): base commit = 120M tokens/month, burst pack = +60M tokens/month (consumable), buffer credits = 20% rollover within quarter. Overage = billed at 1.5x hosted list per-token rate.
- Counter asks from Galewood: capped overage at 50% above committed rate for first 6 months; ability to convert unused quarterly commit to credits or apply to burst consumption. They requested a 3-month ramp schedule: month1 = 30% of commit, month2 = 60%, month3 = 100% with pro-rata credits for early underusage.
- Burst behavior: need predictable burst window (allow spikes up to 3x base for up to 4 hours/day) without immediate throttling. Redwood proposed auto-burst with billing conversion; Galewood wants defined burst buckets and advance notifications when 70% of burst bucket consumed.
- Billing cadence: Galewood prefers monthly invoices with detailed token-level breakdown tied to per-route usage in Console. Procurement pushed back on annual pre-pay.
- Ramp incentives: they asked for a 10% one-time credit if they hit 100% commit by month 3. Redwood's counter: apply onboarding credit and 30-day free burst credit during POC.

Security / legal:
- KBA outstanding: encryption-in-transit/at-rest specifics, HSM/KMS integration timeline, audit log retention windows. Team flagged data residency for EU customers — may want region pinning later.
- They asked for explicit SLA clauses around fallback to hosted (failover) during Dedicated outages.

Open actions / next steps (short):
- AE (Jordan) to send final pricing appendix with two options (token-commit vs GPU-hour commit) by 2026-03-12.
- SE (Maya) to provide a concrete burst-sizing table and sample traffic trace to validate autoscale config by 2026-03-15.
- Legal to receive draft SOW + pricing appendix; procurement to confirm preferred invoice cadence (monthly vs annual) by 2026-03-19.
- Security to complete KBA answer set (INF-1129) and upload to Drive.

Key quotes / signals:
- "We like Redwood's routing and observations — but we need predictable economics when we scale." — VP Product
- "If we can't cap overage or convert commits, procurement will kill the deal." — Head of Finance

Decision drivers: predictable unit economics, VPC isolation, transparent Console telemetry, and a pragmatic ramp/overage policy. Risk: procurement/legal timeline and budget cycle (closing needs to align with their fiscal Q2 approvals).

Suggested AE playbook notes: prioritize a clean two-option commercial: (1) token-commit with quarterly true-up + capped overage for first 6 months; (2) GPU-hour reserved pool with monthly true-up and burst credits. Offer a short-term onboarding credit + 30-day burst buffer to smooth POC-to-dedicated cutover. Keep SE engaged on burst-scenario validation; expedite KBA answers to remove security blocker.
